paper.title: Port Drone Watch: From Oil Sheen to Dispatched Work on the Port's Own Hardware in Germany

scenario: the operator is described by class, never by name: a maritime and ports authority in Germany with two port sites whose retained, docked drone network flies scheduled and on-demand missions under the European specific category, near Seveso perimeters and under GDPR
source: chapter 5 of the paper (the object list and kinds in 5.1, the status vocabularies in 5.2, the recorded form of the Mission in 5.3) and the fourteen typed links and properties of Figure 4; anchors from Table 3, chapter 6.1 and chapter 9.5; the Drone Operator properties and status vocabulary from 10.1; the Coverage Statement vocabulary from 9.4.

objects.label: Mission
objects.anchored_in: The drone operator's mission and fleet system

objects.label: Construction Work
objects.anchored_in: The port's works register (confirmed at the interface survey)

objects.label: Detection
objects.anchored_in: Computed in the model from the drone imagery

objects.label: Work Item
objects.anchored_in: Owned by this system and pushed to the responders' existing work systems

objects.label: Flight Authorisation
objects.anchored_in: Granted by the flight approvers under the European specific category

objects.label: Coverage Statement
objects.anchored_in: Computed in the model from weather groundings

objects.anchored_in: The drone operator's mission and fleet system

properties: Asset type (quay wall, fender, bollard, lock)

objects.label: Drone
objects.anchored_in: The drone operator's mission and fleet system

objects.label: Drone Operator
properties: Authorisations held under the European specific category

objects.label: Weather Observation
objects.anchored_in: The dock weather station or the national meteo service (to confirm, chapter 9.5)

write_paths: the adapter tier (the integration adapter family, schema mapping, provenance stamping and replay into the Kafka backbone, idempotent writes into the model)
the surfaces used by authenticated responders (Keycloak identities in named roles)
work records pushed out to the responders' existing work systems
the governed berth plan layer published back to the port GIS
human_loop: people decide every response: a Detection stays Proposed until a responder confirms, rejects or merges it, every Work Item is acknowledged with reason codes by its named responder role, and flight approvers grant every mission; automatic acts are limited to confirmation re-flights and notification escalation
